why: a small meeting room seen like a stage set: five outlined people round one table, a single plan sheet in the middle; above each head a small thought bubble, folded shut, that only the viewer notices
hands rise one at a time in stepped, drawn-frame timing; on the last hand a hand-lettered stamp, Agreed, lands on the plan sheet while the five folded bubbles stay shut
the stamp peels back off the sheet as time steps backwards; Dana stands at the head of the table and writes the goal on a board behind her, Launch: end of quarter; the other four turn towards it
a speech bubble from the colleague beside Dana; the plan sheet on the table slides a little towards the board, as if the whole table has tilted towards yes

the four folded bubbles open one at a time on their words, each holding one drawn object with its one-word label: a half-ticked checklist, a headset, a sealed envelope, a calendar page with a question mark; the characters cannot see each other's bubbles
slow down here: the camera passes from face to face; each person sees only calm faces and closed bubbles, and on the word only their own bubble shrinks and folds shut
the same hands rise again in stepped timing, now seen from the doubters' side; as each hand goes up, its bubble flattens into a closed lid; Agreed lands on the sheet a second time

a torn-paper jump forward in time, calendar pages tearing off in steps; each private doubt from the opening comes back as the real problem on the same object: the checklist covered in red marks, the headset ringing, the envelope returned
back in the room after the failure: the five people sit in the same places, and the four doubt objects hang above them in a quiet row, none of them touching the table

a black turn card, then the word Groupthink hand-lettered large on a sign that hangs over the meeting room door; under it, a small balance where drive to agree outweighs a hard look on the narrated words
the room again, held in one layout; the three parts light up in turn on their words: the board with Dana's goal, the four folded bubbles, the raised hands; each calms as the next lights

the whole meeting runs backwards in steps, like flipped pages: the stamp lifts, hands come down, the goal on the board erases itself, until the table is clear and the four folded bubbles wait above the same heads

the board behind Dana stays blank; she sits back; the colleague beside her opens his bubble himself and the calendar page with its question mark comes down onto the table as a written note, the first of four
five cards slide out and are written on at the same moment, heads down; turned over together, one card shows the half-ticked checklist; it joins the first note on the table
a small hand-lettered tent card, Critic, is set in front of one person; the headset comes out of the support person's bubble and down onto the table as the third note
the board shows an imagined future page, the plan stamped failed, framed as pretend with a dotted border; the team writes reasons under it, and the sealed envelope comes down as the fourth note

the same five people, the same nervous postures as before; the four notes sit on the table where the empty Agreed stamp was; the plan sheet morphs into an amended plan with the date moved and lines added

a new meeting in the same room, frozen at the quiet after any objections; the four habits sit beside it as four small objects (a blank board, a card, the Critic tent card, the failed page) for the viewer to choose from; a real silent pause

the blank board greys out on its words; cards slide out round the table and are written at once, then turned over together; the doubts appear on the cards at the same moment, so no single person is first
the view widens from Dana's table to a wall calendar of the viewer's week; one meeting slot gets a small hand-lettered tag for a chosen habit

callback to the opening frame, same angle and same five people: where the folded bubbles were, the four notes now sit on the table in front of them, and the Agreed stamp is replaced by the amended plan; the frame rests
